scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude, and we were on a lease. When the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he mentioned in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of cases where people have $250 taken off their deposit just for someone to take three milk crates of stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off. So, I texted and emailed him for two weeks asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump, but he never responded. So, I took most of his stuff to the dump, but he also had around 60 video games for the PS4. I figured I'd sell them. There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party he was at, and we were being polite. Then he asked how the move-out was, and I said it was good. Naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games, but I told him that I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing I can be held accountable for, but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Alright, so I need to figure out if I did the right thing or not. Let's break it down. First, he left without giving proper notice and didn't respond to my messages. I tried to contact him for two weeks, but he ignored me. So, I took his stuff to the dump, which is what the landlord would have done anyway, costing him money. But instead of just dumping them, I sold the video games and made $600. Now, he's upset because he found out, and he's calling me names and wants his money back. Is it wrong to sell his games? Well, legally, I don't think so because he abandoned the stuff, and I was just trying to prevent him from losing money on his deposit. But morally, is it wrong? Did I overstep by selling his personal belongings without his consent? Even though he didn't respond to my messages, maybe I should have made more effort to contact him or find another way to handle his stuff. Also, by selling the games, I gained financially from his belongings. Is that fair? He might feel that I took advantage of his situation. Even though I tried to contact him, maybe I should have considered other options, like donating the games or finding another way to dispose of them without selling them for profit. On the other hand, I prevented him from losing money on his deposit by not letting the landlord take his stuff to the dump. So, in a way, I was helping him by selling the games instead of having his deposit docked. But he's still upset because he feels like I took his stuff without his permission. I'm also thinking about the relationship aspect. We were roommates, and now he's calling me names and being hostile. That's not good for either of us. Maybe I should have handled the situation differently to maintain a better relationship, even if it meant not selling the games. But then again, I was just trying to do the right thing by preventing financial loss for both of us. It's a tough spot because I don't want to be seen as the asshole, but I also don't want to lose money or have a bad relationship with my former roommate. Maybe I should have communicated more clearly or found a middle ground, like letting him know I was going to sell the games and offering him a share of the proceeds. That way, he wouldn't feel like I took advantage of him. But I didn't think of that at the time. In the end, I think I did what I thought was right to prevent financial loss, but maybe I should have considered his feelings more and found a way to involve him in the decision. That way, I wouldn't have ended up in this situation where he's upset and calling me names.
